Patch sales notch 1000 gourds for Wildwood

By Jay Russell · October 7, 2026 · 1 min read

Pumpkin sales at the Wildwood Dads Club’s (WWDC) Pumpkin Patch are scorching hot this year, with more than 1,100 pumpkins, gourds and other items sold in the first 10 days. A big reinforcement, sure to tip the scales, is en route as well; Giant Jack will arrive this week.

When the giant pumpkin arrives patch visitors can pay $1 to guess Giant Jack’s weight. The closest guest will win possession and curbside delivery of the enormous gorgeous gourd for Halloween. Giant Jack will magically vanish from the winner’s home in November, courtesy of the Fuji Melons delivery team.

Patch Papa Matt Derrigo and his seventh-grade daughter, Sara Derrigo, both returned to the Patch this year as WWDC and Wildwood alums. The duo helped create a new fall photo spot for visiting families to create lasting memories. After years of visiting the Patch as an elementary school student, Sara is now helping shape the traditions and experiences for the next generation of Piedmont kids.

Opening weekend and the first full week of sales have substantially outpaced recent years, and this past Sunday brought in more than double the sales of the comparable Sunday last year.

“That growth is especially notable because Patch pricing has stayed largely the same for the past four years, so the increase is coming from more visitors rather than higher prices,” said Patch Papa Brian Fischer.

The high turnout is all the more impressive given this past weekend’s heat wave; temperatures in the 90s didn’t turn families away or smiles from patch visitors upside-down.

As of October 4, the Patch has sold 1,187 total items including 394 decorative pumpkins and gourds. Keeping the Patch open seven days a week, for five weeks requires 156 volunteer shifts and 90 Wildwood parents volunteers have already signed up to make the club’s biggest fundraiser of the year possible.

Mon-Fri: 4:00-6:00 p.m. Sat-Sun: 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m.
